rv.q: Joel Drake Johnson’s riveting play gives that moment of passage a clear and honest voice.
Then we come to Valerie Gorman , who plays Peggy, and is—here’s me trying not to descend into hyperbole—absolutely fantastic.
In the hands of this cast and crew, Four Places reaches deep into the anxieties of aging amidst damaged family bonds.
The story, made up of secrets, lies and misunderstandings, shows us the complex relationships within a family.

This production , under the skillful hand of Director Lauren Berman, allows us to be the perverbial "fly on the wall" as Ellen and Warren pick up their mom for an outing, including a nice luncheon as well as some "quality time together".
